statement: Let V be a vector space over a field K of scalars, and let T: V -> V be a linear transformation. A scalar \lambda \in K is called an eigenvalue of T corresponding to an eigenvector v if there exists a nonzero vector v \in V such that T(v) = \lambda v. For an n x n square matrix A, \lambda is an eigenvalue corresponding to nonzero vector v if A v = \lambda v.

symbols.meaning: Linear transformation mapping V into V
Vector space over a field of scalars K
Square matrix representing a linear transformation

properties.property: The eigenspace E = {v : T(v) = \lambda v} associated with eigenvalue \lambda is the kernel of the linear transformation T - \lambda I.
properties.why: Rearranging the defining equation T(v) = \lambda v gives (T - \lambda I)v = 0.

properties.property: For an n x n matrix A, the eigenvalues are the roots of the characteristic polynomial det(A - \lambda I) = 0.
properties.why: A nontrivial solution v \neq 0 to (A - \lambda I)v = 0 exists if and only if the determinant det(A - \lambda I) vanishes.

properties.property: The eigenvalues of a diagonal or triangular matrix are the elements of its main diagonal.
properties.why: The characteristic polynomial det(A - \lambda I) evaluates directly to the product of the diagonal terms (a_{ii} - \lambda).

properties.property: The sum of the algebraic multiplicities of all distinct eigenvalues equals the dimension n of the matrix.
properties.why: The algebraic multiplicity of each eigenvalue is its multiplicity as a root of the n-th degree characteristic polynomial.

properties.property: Real matrices can yield complex conjugate pairs of eigenvalues and corresponding complex conjugate eigenvectors.
properties.why: Roots of a real polynomial can be complex numbers, which appear in conjugate pairs \lambda and \lambda^*.

assumptions.assumption: The operator T is a linear transformation mapping a vector space V into itself (or A is a square n x n matrix).
assumptions.breaks_when: The transformation is nonlinear or maps between distinct spaces V -> W where V != W.

assumptions.assumption: The eigenvector v associated with an eigenvalue must be nonzero (v != 0).
assumptions.breaks_when: v = 0, which satisfies T(0) = \lambda 0 trivially for every scalar \lambda without defining an eigenvalue.

failure_modes.mode: Defective matrix (geometric multiplicity strictly less than algebraic multiplicity)
failure_modes.signature: The dimension of the eigenspace ker(A - \lambda I) is strictly smaller than the multiplicity of \lambda as a root of det(A - \lambda I) = 0.
failure_modes.cause: A repeated eigenvalue does not possess a sufficient number of linearly independent eigenvectors to span an eigenspace matching its algebraic multiplicity.

failure_modes.mode: Absence of eigenvalues within the base scalar field K
failure_modes.signature: The characteristic polynomial det(A - \lambda I) has no roots in K (for example, a real matrix whose characteristic polynomial has strictly complex roots).
failure_modes.cause: The base field K is not algebraically closed.
